commit.message: fix(verify): fail closed without webhook secret

intent: Close the bounded WP-0S direct GitHub App signature prerequisite by making VerifyWebhookHandler reject every webhook when DHARMA_VERIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, while preserving valid HMAC-SHA256 admission and invalid-signature rejection. This is a fail-closed ingress correction only; it makes no production availability, deployment, complete-security, or Phase 0 closure claim.

honest_blockers: Deployment status is BLOCKED_OPERATOR: this packet does not inspect credentials or establish whether a separate host or VPS runs this API.
Observed evidence supports NOT_DEPLOYED only for the already-audited local Mac and GitHub deployment surfaces; it cannot be generalized to unobserved hosts.
This direct handler correction does not alter production startup behavior, bearer authentication, network exposure, deployment state, or any Phase 1-7 surface.

The first sealed closeout rejected the pytest-based negative control because its jail could not import pytest; the replacement is dependency-free, behaviorally invokes the mutated handler, and reserves exit 3 for every setup failure.

The full caller command python3 -m pytest tests/test_verify_api.py tests/test_api_auth.py -q passed 65 tests locally but its existing API lifespan writes project-relative .dharma state; those ignored artifacts were moved outside the isolated clone, and the sealed packet gate remains side-effect-free while hosted CI must repeat the full callers.
Hosted exact-head CI, independent review, resolution of blocking feedback, human merge authority, and the remaining Titanium Phase 0 DAG stay required.
interface_mismatches: VerifyWebhookHandler.verify_signature currently returns True when DHARMA_VERIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, even though the API route already maps a failed signature result to HTTP 401 and production-shaped middleware separately treats absent verification material as unavailable.
session_entry.rollback: Revert github_app.py, its focused tests, and this packet together. Rollback restores the known fail-open missing-secret behavior and must not be represented as safe webhook ingress.
